key_insight: This paper argues that AI research and deployment should be better aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), so the field produces more socially beneficial outcomes rather than optimizing only technical metrics. The main takeaway is a shift from AI capability-first development to impact-first, sustainability-oriented AI design.
problem_solved: AI progress is often evaluated by benchmark performance, while its broader societal, environmental, and policy impacts are underweighted. This paper addresses the gap between fast-moving AI innovation and the need to direct AI toward measurable sustainable development outcomes.
method: Frames AI development around the Sustainable Development Goals as a guiding policy and research objective.
Synthesizes how AI can be redirected toward high-impact domains such as health, education, climate, and inequality reduction.
Highlights the need for evaluation and governance structures that reward real-world social value, not just model accuracy.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper encourages building systems that are useful, responsible, and aligned with real-world needs. It matters because future AI success will increasingly depend on whether models create measurable positive impact beyond benchmark scores.
visual_elements: A hub-and-spoke diagram linking AI capabilities to the 17 SDGs
Before/after pipeline showing 'benchmark-driven AI' versus 'SDG-aligned AI'
Icons for major impact domains such as health, climate, education, and equality
A roadmap or framework graphic showing research, deployment, and governance layers
paper_title: Realigning AI technology towards the Sustainable Development Goals
paper_authors: Rundong Feng, Ziming Li, Bojie Fu, Huadong Guo, Jianguo Liu
